question: What did sponsors do with companies like Punctual Pros?
html:
What sponsors did with Punctual Pros peers

Across 34 cases from 1996 to 2026, the best home-services exits followed six steps in roughly the same order. Punctual Pros has done the early steps but is behind on add-on cadence and has no clear data on the later ones (value creation cases).

The common sequence

  • Operator team at entry. Alpine named Apex's CEO and CFO on launch day in July 2019. American Capital gave Service Experts' returning CEO about 10% ownership (value creation cases). Trivest hired Kurt Bratton at TurnPoint, and Investcorp hired Ken Haines at Wrench (home-services case studies).
  • Early, nearby first add-on. The median was about 7 months after entry across 11 dated cases (value creation cases).
  • Steady tuck-ins. Sponsors closed roughly one every three to five months. Trivest did 16 at TurnPoint, Huron did 13 at Sciens, and BSP did nine at Smith + Howard (value creation cases).
  • One operating system. CenterOak ran a single IT system at Service Champions, and Wrench books online at 99% of locations on ServiceTitan (value creation cases).
  • Recurring membership revenue. Champions grew from about 60,000 to about 150,000 members, roughly 83 per technician. It sold to Blackstone at a reported ~18.5x, a press estimate (home-services case studies).
  • Own the technician pipeline. Examples include Horizon's training center, Apex's academies and Sila's 2026 academy purchase (home-services case studies).

What went wrong elsewhere

Horizon, Any Hour and TurnPoint added brands faster than they integrated them. Horizon was lender-owned by 2026, Any Hour is on PIK and marked at 89, and TurnPoint is on PIK and changed CEO (home-services case studies). Few sponsors disclose entry or exit multiples, so return comparisons are thin (value creation cases).

Punctual Pros against the sequence

BSP entered on Apr 3, 2024, about 31 months ago (BSP firm profile).

StepPunctual Pros status
Operator teamFounder CEO in place. The recommended next hire is an integrator COO (home-services case studies)
First add-onHorvath in month 8, in line with peers
Tuck-in cadenceOne out-of-state add-on so far (Punctual Pros nationwide plan). This is behind the 3-5 month pace
One systemOn ServiceTitan since Sept 2024 through Authority Brands
Memberships~6,500 members and ~85 technicians (est., planning assumption). That is about 76 members per technician (est.)
Technician pipelineNo data in context

The nationwide plan's 36-month target is ~$100M revenue and ~$16M EBITDA (est.), modelled on Smith + Howard's ~4x growth. That target assumes Phase 1 closes 1-2 tuck-ins from a 61-company screen. Seventeen PE sponsors are competing for the same founders (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

Next actions

  • Confirm actual member counts, technician headcount and renewal rates from ServiceTitan, and replace the planning assumptions.
  • Rank the 61-company screen and set a target of one close every three to five months. Start with the 144 PA and 51 MD priority ZIP codes.
  • Scope an integrator COO role before the add-on pace speeds up, to avoid the Horizon and TurnPoint pattern.
  • Collect technician hiring, training and attrition data to decide whether a training academy is worth building.

## The common sequence

- **Operator team at entry.** Alpine named Apex's CEO and CFO on launch day in July 2019. American Capital gave Service Experts' returning CEO about 10% ownership (value creation cases). Trivest hired Kurt Bratton at TurnPoint, and Investcorp hired Ken Haines at Wrench (home-services case studies).
- **Early, nearby first add-on.** The median was about 7 months after entry across 11 dated cases (value creation cases).
- **Steady tuck-ins.** Sponsors closed roughly one every three to five months. Trivest did 16 at TurnPoint, Huron did 13 at Sciens, and BSP did nine at Smith + Howard (value creation cases).
- **One operating system.** CenterOak ran a single IT system at Service Champions, and Wrench books online at 99% of locations on ServiceTitan (value creation cases).
- **Recurring membership revenue.** Champions grew from about 60,000 to about 150,000 members, roughly 83 per technician. It sold to Blackstone at a reported ~18.5x, a press estimate (home-services case studies).
- **Own the technician pipeline.** Examples include Horizon's training center, Apex's academies and Sila's 2026 academy purchase (home-services case studies).

## What went wrong elsewhere

Horizon, Any Hour and TurnPoint added brands faster than they integrated them. Horizon was lender-owned by 2026, Any Hour is on PIK and marked at 89, and TurnPoint is on PIK and changed CEO (home-services case studies). Few sponsors disclose entry or exit multiples, so return comparisons are thin (value creation cases).

## Punctual Pros against the sequence

BSP entered on Apr 3, 2024, about 31 months ago (BSP firm profile).

| Step | Punctual Pros status |
|---|---|
| Operator team | Founder CEO in place. The recommended next hire is an integrator COO (home-services case studies) |
